description:
Found while building bd-4et. Observed for real, not theorised.

A daemon whose `daemon.sock` had been removed out from under it SURVIVED 10+
seconds of SIGTERM and only died to SIGKILL. A healthy daemon on the same box
exits 60/54/54 ms after SIGTERM (measured on a 55-bead store), so this is not
slow shutdown — it is not handling the signal at all.

Most likely wedged in its accept loop: blocked accepting on a socket that no
longer exists, so it never reaches the point where it would notice the shutdown
flag.

Mitigated but NOT fixed by bd-4et: `bn daemon stop` now polls actual process
liveness and escalates SIGTERM -> SIGKILL, so a user is no longer stuck. But
SIGKILL means no clean shutdown — no WAL checkpoint, no orderly socket/meta
cleanup — so we are relying on crash recovery every time this path fires. Not
where you want to be for a tracker.

Real fix is in the daemon: make the accept loop interruptible and the signal
handler effective even when the socket has gone. Worth checking whether it
notices socket deletion at all, since that is also a "should I exit?" signal.

How to reproduce: start a daemon, `rm` its `daemon.sock`, then SIGTERM it and
watch it sit there.
title: kopi-beans: an orphaned daemon ignores SIGTERM indefinitely (socket deleted underneath it)
